synthesis_caveats: Input files read (15, matching every target in config/sources.yml): industry-openai, industry-anthropic, industry-google-deepmind, industry-meta-ai, industry-microsoft, industry-sakana-ai, evaluator-metr, evaluator-epoch-ai, evaluator-uk-ai-security-institute, academia-mit-csail, academia-stanford-hai, academia-cmu-ri, academia-alan-turing-institute, academia-utokyo-riken-aip, wildcard. The synthesis agent has no directory-listing tool, so filenames were located from the naming conventions in .claude/agents/*.md. Any extra file that does not follow those conventions would have been missed.

8 of 15 collectors returned items (29 items total). Google DeepMind, Meta AI, Microsoft, Sakana AI, UK AISI, Stanford HAI, UTokyo/RIKEN AIP and wildcard returned zero items because of DNS or fetch failures. Their collectors say this is an access gap, not proof that nothing was published.

Almost every item is primary-inferred or secondary-source, built from search snippets. Only 4 Anthropic items are primary-confirmed. Every theme below rests on unverified figures and should be treated as tentative.
Several Anthropic items (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-28) and one METR item (2026-10-22) fall before the 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-07 window. Collectors included them as the latest available or as context.

No cross-category divergent points could be supported by item IDs this week. Any tension below is only one source's report about another party, and the other party's own statement was not collected. It is noted here instead of being entered as a divergent point.

Theme 'AI R&D acceleration measurement': METR reports (item metr-2026-11-05-review-anthropic-risk-report-rd) that Anthropic's public and private reports sometimes describe the AI contribution differently. Anthropic's August 2026 Risk Report was not collected as an item, so no divergent point was built.

Theme 'AI R&D acceleration measurement': the two METR posts give different figures (about 2x with roughly 80% attributed to AI, versus about 1.5x to 1.9x). The collector notes that the two posts use different data and methods, and warns against reading them as contradictory without reading both. They are therefore not entered as a divergence.

themes.theme: AI R&D acceleration measurement (METR assessment of Anthropic)

convergent_points.claim: Both METR posts dated 2026-11-05 estimate that AI is speeding up Anthropic's capability R&D (above 1x relative to an earlier baseline), while METR calls the estimates uncertain. Single source (METR): this is agreement within one evaluator, not across sources.
METR broadly agrees that direct catastrophic risk from automated R&D by Anthropic models as of 15 July 2026 was low. Single source (METR).

An industry lab and an evaluator both published material this week on large-scale AI compute and data-center buildout. OpenAI covered community and reporting standards for its campuses. Epoch covered estimates of compute shipments and facility power capacity. The overlap is in topic only; the items make different kinds of claims.

themes.theme: AI applied to scientific and life-science work

convergent_points.claim: Two industry labs published material on applying AI to life-science or scientific research: OpenAI's wet-lab agent benchmark, and Anthropic's drug-development partnerships and expanded AI for Science program. Industry sources only; no evaluator or academic item on this topic was collected.
